newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine tells Tatton to stick with Hamilton.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine tells Tatton to stick with Hamilton.

text.p: Britain's deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine on Wednesday told the northern England constituency of Tatton to stick with Neil Hamilton, the MP embroiled in a cash for questions scandal.
Neil Hamilton was confirmed on Tuesday night as the Conservative candidate for Tatton after 182 people supported him and 100 either abstained or voted against him.

Heseltine told BBC radio that an independent Conservative candidate, who may be put up by disgruntled local Tories, could split the vote and allow BBC war correspondent Martin Bell, who he called a Labour/Liberal candidate, to win the seat.
"It seems too perverse...to put up someone unknown, unidentified which would only have the effect of putting a Labour/Liberal coalition candidate into the House of Commons," he said.
Martin Bell will run as an anti-corruption candidate in a move designed to force Hamilton to stand down. The Labour and Liberal candidates are set to stand aside in Tatton.
Hamilton denies allegations that he accepted money to ask parliamentary questions and has steadfastly refused to step down because of the scandal.
"I think they should give Hamilton the benefit of the doubt," Heseltine said. "We do have a system in this country where people are innocent until proven guilty."
Pollsters say the sleaze issue is preventing the ruling Conservatives from eating in to Labour's lead of 20 points and more in the opinion polls.
And the Hamilton/Bell showdown will keep the sleaze issue at the forefront of the three weeks left of the election campaign.
"You will get the Labour and Liberal parties making capital out of this," Heseltine admitted.
